_: ENV-3 · the declared migration state of each environment.
This file is NOT a ledger. supabase_migrations.schema_migrations is the ledger
and the only authority on what IS applied. This file declares what SHOULD be
applied where, so CI has something true to compare the ledger against.
The comparison is two-way, exactly as known-violations.json is: a version
applied without being declared here fails, and a version declared here without
being applied fails. The frontier can only move when reality and intent move
together.
Semantics, and there are only four rules:
applied_through  the frontier. Expected = every authored version <= this,
minus anything in `excluded`.
excluded         authored versions AT OR BELOW the frontier that are
deliberately not applied here. Each needs a reason and the
gate that releases it.
pending          authored versions ABOVE the frontier, deliberately not yet
applied. Each needs a reason and the gate that releases it.
every authored version must appear in exactly one of those three states.
Silence is not a state -- an undeclared migration fails.
Only QA is declared. Production's history is reconciled by RELEASE_GATES row
9B.2 (G-09), which owns dumping and reconciling its ledger and enumerates its
known divergences in 9B.3. Declaring a production frontier here before that
work exists would be inventing state this repository cannot yet stand behind.

187.reason: Booking slot integrity. A client cannot UPDATE coach_availability (coach-only write policies), so the app's is_booked write after a booking matched zero rows: booked slots stayed on offer and were booked again, and nothing in the schema allowed only one live call per slot. Adds a partial UNIQUE index (one non-cancelled call per slot), a BEFORE trigger that locks the slot and refuses 23505 when it is flagged booked or already held (23514 for another coach's slot; the call takes the slot's own time), and an AFTER trigger that keeps is_booked in step with claims and releases. No backfill: existing flags are left and respected. QA pre-flight 2026-11-14: 0 slots with two live calls. Locally replay-verified (supabase/tests/local/integrity_187_192_replay.sh, 34 assertions for 187-192: pre-fix 24 FAIL, post-fix all PASS, also applied directly on the 181 frontier, twice). NOT applied to QA.
187.gate: An owner-approved QA apply window, then the live QA suites and CI. Independent of 182-186 (replay-verified on the 181 frontier). Consequence to accept at apply time: a second booking of a taken slot now fails with 23505 where it used to succeed; the app's booking screen should map 23505 to 'that time was just taken' (separate app PR).

188.reason: Class seat integrity. live_class_service.dart ran Module 13 (full -> waitlisted; a cancellation promotes the earliest waitlisted booking) in the client, where RLS shows a client only its own bookings: capacity was never enforced (every booking confirmed), classes.current_enrolled was never updated (coach-only writes; 3 classes on QA disagree with their bookings), and waitlist promotion never happened (a client cannot see other users' waitlisted bookings; a caller who can, such as the class's coach, had its update blocked and still sent "You're In!"). BEFORE trigger assigns confirmed/waitlisted counted over all bookings under a lock on the class row (capacity coalesce(max_capacity, 20), as the app); AFTER trigger promotes the earliest waitlisted booking(s) into released seats with the same notification, now true, and recomputes current_enrolled; one-time recompute of current_enrolled (derived counter, no booking changed). QA pre-flight 2026-11-14: 0 classes over capacity. Locally replay-verified (see 187). NOT applied to QA.
188.gate: An owner-approved QA apply window, then the live QA suites and CI. Independent of 182-187.
